items.notes: Cited sections state expand/migrate/contract is gated after a compatibility window and old readers are retained; the nonclaim on automatic DB consistency matches.
Demand-skew and shard-key evidence shows averages hide popular-resource contention and that skew/cardinality must be tested explicitly.
The diagram directly shows Rollback leading to Legacy on drain completion and only accepted cutover ending at the target.
The only cited section names linked legacy failure mechanisms but not the healthy-shard miss mechanism; abstention is consistent with the supplied excerpt.
Excerpts name Wedge as a component-coupling feedback mechanism but do not state how it detected or reported dependencies; abstention is supported.
GitOps evidence says the reconciler applies declared state; the business-outcome section says a clean diff does not prove durable writes, effects or contracts.
The identity section directly recommends a stable ID plus versioned description and a simple Markdown table; the integrated route supports cross-view consistency.
Shard ownership denies independent hot-key throughput and the quorum section explains majority-vote arithmetic; the write-throughput conclusion is a fair synthesis.
Cited sections state ambiguous in-flight outcomes and the policy required before promoting a writer; catch-up and reconciliation follow from that.
Trace-identity and retry sections distinguish trace or attempt from logical operation; the logging section supports the audit-record limitation.
Outbox evidence establishes that the broker is outside the DB commit and pending intent must still be published; relay cleanup is consistent with the cited pattern.
The cited Splitter decision is nearly verbatim: a known total or an explicit release rule/expiry prevents a silent partial result.
Controlled Cutover requires planned downtime after writes pause; the resharding section requires client, store, replica and ownership consistency.
Broker atomicity and inbox-local-transaction evidence support at-least-once delivery and consumer deduplication.
The cited Claim Check section gives only justification and lifecycle conditions, not the failure mode when a token precedes durable payload storage.
Insufficient-evidence, statistical-validity, provenance and uncertainty sections jointly support every stated claim.
Verification-versus-validation plus the five-layer and worked-separation evidence directly support the distinction.
The structural gate lists the identifier and link checks; diagram and ten-rules sections support hash binding and read-only pattern links.
The correlated-input section plus the staged-result and experiment-design details match the stated shift, lag, capacity and range values.
Resource controls and the 20-vs-24 comparison are supported, but no queue discipline is named; the answer itself concedes that only part of the question is covered.
